newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Slovakia to consider Hungary's committee proposal.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia to consider Hungary's committee proposal.

text.p: Slovakia will consider setting up a Slovak-Hungarian intergovernmental committee to oversee the two countries' basic treaty, as proposed on Wednesday by Hungary's foreign minister, officials said.
"The Hungarian side would not have to wait long for an answer," Pavol Hamzik, Slovak Foreign Minister, told a news conference on Wednesday, after talks with his Hungarian counterpart, Laszlo Kovacs.
The Slovak and Hungarian prime ministers signed a basic relations treaty in 1995, which was ratified by the Slovak parliament almost a year later.
Bilateral relations have been strained over a recent Hungarian conference at which government officials signed a declaration supporting the autonomy of ethnic Hungarians in the region.
Slovakia has an ethnic Hungarian minority of around 600,000 living near the southern border with Hungary.
"The committee proposed by us would further the implementation of the treaty... which is expected to be a long process," said Kovacs.
Hamzik, answering a question, said he did not see any technical difficulty in setting up such a committee, but declined to say whether it would be desirable.
"At this point, I can only say we have to consider the proposal," Hamzik said.
